sections.title: Form and colour
sections.text: Red bog-moss forms slender shoots in low patches or small hummocks. Plants are often red, but may be mixed red and green; shoots are small, and the branch leaves are roughly 1 mm long.

sections.title: Habitat and identification
sections.text: It grows in acidic bogs, heaths and wet woodland. Colour and growth form vary, and separating Sphagnum species can require microscopic characters; the plate’s compact red cushions are consistent with the species but are not by themselves diagnostic.

sections.title: Use and safety
sections.text: Like other peat mosses, it contributes to peat formation and stores water. It is not presented here as food; harvesting wild bog moss can damage sensitive peatland habitat.
